steps.say: Let the AI app you already use work in {product} for you - the same buttons you press, as you.

Connect your AI lets an app such as Claude or ChatGPT work in {product} for you, for tests and demos: look things up and press the same buttons you would, as you. Signing in, payments and other people's steps stay with people.

In your AI app, open its connectors and add a custom one. Paste this portal's address - the Copy button puts it on your clipboard. Press Connect: a window opens on this site, you sign in with your normal account and press Allow. No key, no terminal.
The status line turns green the moment your AI app first asks something, and names the app and when it last asked.
Check runs a real question through the server - it answers, it lists its tools, a tool replies - and says in plain words which step fails, if any.
Every connected app is listed with how many questions it asked. Disconnect stops it at once, and asks first.

These are the tools an AI app may use: reads look things up, changes press one of {product}'s own buttons, and the steps marked for a person are never done by a tool. Each can be switched off in People and access under Connect your AI.
An app that cannot sign in - a script, or Claude Code - can use a key instead. Keys are made under For developers, shown once, and revoked there.
